item.title: How HalfPe is building a marketplace for surplus inventory at 50% off
item.description:
Founded by serial entrepreneur Venu G Somineni, HalfPe connects retailers and brands with consumers looking for discounted products, using a seller-owned inventory model and AI-led operations.
India's ecommerce platforms regularly offer discounts during sales and festivals. HalfPe.com is taking
item.content:encoded:
A product sitting unsold in a warehouse can still be exactly what a household needs. HalfPe.com connects those two sides with a simple promise: every listed product at least 50% below MRP, throughout the year. For shoppers, the attraction is everyday savings. For retailers and brands, it is another route to turn unsold stock into revenue.

The platform focuses on surplus inventory: new, unsold products that retailers and brands need to clear as new stock arrives. It aims to provide an organized, consumer-facing marketplace for this inventory while allowing sellers to recover value from products that might otherwise remain unsold or be liquidated through bulk channels.

HalfPe was founded by Venu G Somineni, with Tirumalarao Chamalla as co-founder. Somineni, a former Microsoft employee and serial entrepreneur, has founded five technology businesses. He has spent 15 years building impactful businesses from India and the US. The company also has some of the most famous business executives, including Umasankar Nistala and Rajkumar Velagapudi, on board.

The company operates with an AI-first team of 40 employees and says it processes more than 5,000 orders a day, with most orders coming from Tier II and Tier III markets.

“Every other platform asks how much discount to give,” Somineni says. “We asked a different question: what happens if half price is simply where India starts shopping?”

Addressing the surplus inventory market

India's retail market is estimated at around $1.2 trillion. According to the industry estimates cited by HalfPe, nearly 20% of retail inventory remains unsold each year, representing a potential surplus pool of approximately $240 billion.

This includes products such as previous-generation phones, out-of-season clothing, and unsold festival gift packs.

For retailers and brands, clearing this inventory can be difficult. Large discounts on their own platforms may affect brand positioning and create pricing concerns among customers who purchased the same products at full price.

As a result, surplus stock is often sold through bulk liquidation channels at substantially reduced prices or held in warehouses, where its value may decline over time.

Organised off-price retail has developed into a large global sector, but HalfPe sees an opportunity to build a dedicated consumer-facing marketplace for surplus products in India as ecommerce continues to expand.

Partnerships and a seller-owned inventory model

HalfPe says it has signed master-level agreements with Flipkart for surplus inventory across multiple categories, Reliance Retail for fashion, Zepto for surplus generated by its dark stores, and many other top brands and conglomerates in India.

According to the company, the first consignments from Reliance Retail are being scheduled.

The platform allows these companies to sell surplus inventory through a separate channel without offering the same discounts on their primary storefronts.

Unlike conventional inventory-led retailers, HalfPe does not purchase the products it sells.

Inventory remains with sellers and is either shipped directly from the warehouses of more than 700 vendors through a nationwide logistics network or held on consignment at HalfPe's consolidated warehouses in the National Capital Region (NCR), Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.

The company is also rolling out hyperlocal delivery through partner stores in major cities.

Vendors receive payment when their products are sold, while HalfPe earns a fee on completed sales. This allows the platform to operate without purchasing inventory or tying up capital in unsold goods.

The company uses AI-based order routing to manage dispatch and fulfilment.

Targeting value-conscious consumers

HalfPe's marketplace lists products from more than 250 brands, including Bata, boAt, Lakmé, Tata, and Penguin.

According to the company, every product is new and listed at a minimum 50% discount on its MRP, regardless of the category or time of year.

The platform aims to simplify discount shopping by replacing varying promotional offers, coupon codes, and limited-period sales with a fixed minimum discount.

Its proposition is particularly focused on middle-class and value-conscious households.

HalfPe describes this approach through the idea that saving money on purchases is another form of earning. It believes a consistent discount can help households reduce their spending on regular purchases.

The company says most of its daily orders come from Tier II and Tier III cities, including markets such as Vijayawada and Indore, where it sees demand for affordable branded products.

It also considers these markets important to the next phase of ecommerce growth in India.

Taking the model offline with Half Price Days

HalfPe is extending its marketplace model to physical retail through Half Price Days, a city-level shopping exhibition where participating brands offer products at a minimum 50% discount.

Customers can examine and purchase products at the venue, while the same inventory is made available on HalfPe.com to shoppers across India for the duration of the event.

The company has organized editions in Tirupati and Vijayawada, which it says attracted substantial footfall.

Bengaluru is the next planned destination, with the company positioning the event as the city's largest retail expo. HalfPe plans to take the format to other major cities, including Visakhapatnam, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kochi, Mumbai and Delhi.

Participating vendors do not pay stall fees. Instead, HalfPe earns revenue when products are sold.

The company says these events also help it acquire customers and onboard vendors, with surplus inventory remaining available on its online marketplace after the exhibitions conclude.

It plans to use the format during festive shopping periods and aims to organise Half Price Days weekends across major Indian cities.

Using agentic AI to manage operations

HalfPe uses agentic artificial intelligence (AI) to automate parts of its marketplace operations.

According to the company, autonomous software agents onboard vendor catalogues, check whether listings meet the minimum 50% discount requirement, analyze demand, and route orders through the available fulfilment network.

These systems handle repetitive operational tasks, allowing the company's 40-member team to focus on decisions that require human intervention.

HalfPe is also preparing for the growth of agentic commerce, in which AI assistants help consumers compare products, evaluate prices, and potentially place orders.

As consumers increasingly use AI assistants, including ChatGPT, for shopping recommendations, the company is structuring its catalogue to make its products searchable by these systems.

HalfPe believes its consistent discount model could make its listings attractive to AI-driven shopping tools that compare products primarily on value.

Building an off-price retail platform

HalfPe’s business model is based on using existing surplus inventory rather than subsidising discounts to attract customers.

Retailers and brands offer markdowns to recover value from unsold stock, customers purchase products at reduced prices, and HalfPe earns a fee on each sale.

The company believes this approach can provide a sustainable pricing advantage as its network of brands, vendors and customers grows.

It also sees an environmental benefit in finding buyers for surplus products that might otherwise be discarded, destroyed or left unused.

HalfPe was recognised as Ecommerce Platform of the Year 2026 by HT Media and Emerging Retailer of the Year 2026 by The Economic Times.

The company aims to expand its position in India's off-price retail market by helping brands and retailers sell existing inventory to value-conscious consumers.

“The middle class built modern India,” Somineni says. “HalfPe is how modern India pays them back — 50% at a time.”

item.title: Bengaluru leads India in AI startup funding: Innovation Report 2026
item.description: $85 billion raised, a growing AI ecosystem and a strong deep-tech pipeline. The Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 maps the city's startup growth as Karnataka looks to spread its tech ambitions beyond the capital.
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru's position as India's technology hub is increasingly being shaped by artificial intelligence and deep tech. The city accounts for 36.3% of the country's native AI startup funding and is home to 71% of India's AI and deep tech unicorns created since 2023.

These findings feature in the Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026, released by Karnataka IT and BT Minister Priyank M. Kharge on November 18 at the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, held at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC).

Prepared by the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) with 3one4 Capital and data from Tracxn, the report examines Bengaluru's startup ecosystem across capital, talent, unicorns, policy and six frontier technology sectors.

AI and deep tech lead the way

Bengaluru has seen 1,556 deep tech startups founded since 2010, of which 1,319 remain active and funded. Together, these companies have raised US$3.77 billion.

The city also has 799 native AI startups, with 764 active and funded. Its share of India's native AI funding is higher than that of any other city.

Bengaluru's overall startup ecosystem has raised approximately US$85 billion since 2010, accounting for 47% of all venture funding raised by Indian startups. The city has 3,810 active, funded startups founded since 2010, compared with 1,982 in Mumbai.

Its 57 unicorns are valued at US$211 billion, representing 44% of India's unicorn count and 55.3% of their combined valuation. Bengaluru is also home to 212 soonicorns, accounting for 36% of India's total.

Capital and exits strengthen ecosystem

The report points to growing participation from domestic investors. Around 52% of capital raised by Category I and II alternative investment funds (AIFs) now comes from domestic investors.

Bengaluru has 75 Category I AIFs, representing 21% of India's total, and around 300 venture capital firms operate in Karnataka.

The city has also recorded 16 Bengaluru-linked company listings since November 2024, together valued at approximately US$42 billion at listing. Startups in the ecosystem take an average of 8.2 years from founding to exit, compared with the global average of 11.1 years.

Women entrepreneurs are another part of the ecosystem. Nearly 30% of India's active, funded women-led startups in deep tech and native AI were founded in Bengaluru. These companies have collectively raised US$323.65 million.

Karnataka looks beyond Bengaluru

The report also examines the State's efforts to expand its technology ecosystem beyond the capital.

Since 2017, the ELEVATE grant-in-aid programme has supported 1,479 startups with Rs 393.58 crore, with 38.6% of the beneficiaries based beyond Bengaluru. Karnataka has also established a Rs 75 crore Beyond Bengaluru Cluster Seed Fund and is developing Global Technology Centres in Mysuru, Hubballi and Belagavi.

The Rs 1,000 crore Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP) aims to generate five lakh jobs over five years.

Releasing the report, Kharge said Karnataka's next priority was to extend its technology strengths to other parts of the State.

"The Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 shows how far Karnataka's founders have come and how much more they can build from here. Our next task is to make sure a world-class AI, quantum or semiconductor company can grow just as well in Kalaburagi, Hubballi or Mangaluru," he said.

He added that deep tech requires patient investment and that Karnataka would continue supporting the sector.

Shri Sharath Bachegowda, Chairman of KEONICS, said the findings reaffirm Karnataka's leadership in AI and deep tech while pointing to opportunities to expand innovation across the State.

Dr Manjula N, Secretary of the Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, said the focus was now on helping startups move from early support to scale through government procurement, patient capital and stronger research commercialisation.

BV Naidu, Chairman of KDEM, said the report offers investors, global capability centres (GCCs) and founders a data-backed view of Karnataka's technology ecosystem.

The Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 is available on the KDEM website.

item.title: Debate brews over Sarvam hosting Chinese AI models; Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here

item.content:encoded:
Dear Reader, 

Sarvam hosts Chinese AI models on Indian infrastructure. The move has sparked debate over AI sovereignty. More on this later in the edition.

Speaking of AI, Nvidia’s board has no intention of reinstating Jensen Huang as chief executive, chair Harvey Jones said on the chipmaker’s earnings call on Wednesday. His remarks came hours after Huang said he would be honoured to return if the board believed it was in the company's best interest.

As for its earnings report, the company also said its net income more than doubled to $65.3 billion for the quarter ended October 25, 2026, from $31.9 billion a year earlier.

Apollo Hospitals is using an AI agent developed with Microsoft to speed up reviews of patient falls, medication errors and readmissions. The hospital says the system has coincided with fewer recorded incidents, although this does not establish that AI alone caused the decline.

The newly-developed Daily Tiered Huddle agent supports clinical-governance teams. It brings together hospital records, flags cases, builds patient timelines and prompts clinicians for missing details. The agent also suggests assessments for doctors to check and amend.

In other news, domestic and global institutional investors such as Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund and BlackRock have increased their stake in Groww by acquiring shares worth Rs 1,905 crore, per block deal data on NSE.

In today’s newsletter, we will talk about 

  • Debate brews over Sarvam hosting Chinese AI models
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here

Here’s your trivia for today: Originally named DMA Design when it created the first Grand Theft Auto in 1997, the Scottish studio behind the franchise is now known as Rockstar... what?

Artificial intelligence

Debate brews over Sarvam hosting Chinese AI models

With its newly-launched Token Factory offering access to models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Z.ai, alongside its own models and Google’s Gemma, Bengaluru-based Sarvam AI is positioning itself as an AI developer and an inference provider. 

The move has attracted criticism from those who believe a company backed by public resources should prioritise original Indian research.

Key takeaways:

  • Token Factory is an inference platform, which provides the computing infrastructure required to run trained AI models and generate responses.
  • The criticism about Sarvam AI centres on the distinction between hosting AI and developing it.
  • Hemant Mohapatra, a partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the launch, pointing out that international inference providers are already making money by hosting foreign models in India.

Gaming

GTA VI is finally here

More than 13 years after the release of Grand Theft Auto V, GTA VI is finally here. The game is exclusive to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, with no release planned for PC, PS4, or Xbox One.

PlayStation India lists the Standard Edition at Rs 5,999 and the Ultimate Edition at Rs 7,499. Both come with the Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+, Rockstar's subscription service.

Game on:

  • Indian players do not have to wait for a courier. Quick-commerce platform Blinkit announced on its official account that GTA 6 is now available on its app, with delivery in minutes.
  • Pre-loading opened on 12 November. On the PS5, the game needs at least 212 GB of free space, according to PlayStation's store page.
  • Rockstar has not announced a PC version. That matters in India, where many serious gamers play on PCs and gaming laptops because consoles are expensive.

  • Profits: Public shareholders in Paytm’s parent company, One 97 Communications, have seen their investments grow roughly 1.7x over the past five years. The rally, which pushed the fintech giant's shares to a new high, reflects a major expansion in both retail ownership and institutional backing since its market debut.

item.title: Doom-scrolling detox: 7 Simple rules to reclaim your attention
item.description: Discover seven simple rules for a doom-scrolling detox to reduce screen time, improve focus, protect your mental space and build healthier digital habits.
item.content:encoded:
You pick up your smartphone to check one notification, and before you know it, 40 minutes have passed.

One video leads to another, a quick news update turns into endless scrolling, and suddenly, you have spent a significant part of your day consuming information you never intended to look for.

Even when you realise how much time has passed, putting your phone down can feel surprisingly difficult.

This habit is commonly known as doom-scrolling, the tendency to spend excessive time scrolling through negative news, social media updates and endless online content.

While staying informed and entertained is not necessarily a problem, constantly consuming information without a clear purpose can affect your concentration, sleep and ability to stay present.

The solution is not necessarily to delete every social media application or stop using your phone altogether. Instead, it is about becoming more intentional with your screen time and creating boundaries that allow you to regain control of your attention.

7 Simple rules to break the doom-scrolling habit

1. Stop checking your phone first thing in the morning

How you spend the first few minutes after waking up can influence how you approach the rest of your day. Many people reach for their phones immediately after opening their eyes, checking messages, notifications, news updates and social media feeds before even getting out of bed.

This habit exposes your mind to a constant stream of information before you have had the opportunity to focus on your own priorities. You may begin your day reacting to other people's activities, opinions and problems instead of deciding what deserves your attention.

Try creating a phone-free morning routine. Give yourself the first 30 minutes after waking up without social media or unnecessary notifications. Use this time to freshen up, pray, exercise, read or plan your day. You can also keep your phone away from your bedside table to make the habit easier to maintain.

The objective is not to avoid technology completely but to begin your day with intention rather than immediately entering the digital world.

2. Set a daily limit for social media

One of the easiest ways to reduce doom-scrolling is to become more aware of how much time you spend on social media. Without a clear limit, a few minutes of browsing can quickly turn into hours of unnecessary screen time.

Start by checking your phone's screen-time report to understand which applications consume most of your attention. Once you identify the platforms where you spend the most time, set realistic daily limits using your phone's built-in screen-time settings.

For example, if you spend three hours scrolling through social media, reducing that time gradually may be more sustainable than trying to stop completely overnight. You could begin by cutting down 20 to 30 minutes and use that time for reading, walking or another meaningful activity.

Remember that the purpose of setting limits is not to create another source of pressure. It is to make sure that social media remains a small part of your day rather than becoming the centre of it.

3. Turn off unnecessary notifications

Every notification creates an opportunity for distraction. A message alert, promotional update, social media like or breaking news notification can interrupt whatever you are doing and encourage you to pick up your phone.

Even when you do not open every notification, constantly seeing them can make you feel the need to check your device. This can gradually affect your ability to concentrate on tasks that require uninterrupted attention.

Take a few minutes to review your notification settings. Turn off alerts from applications that do not require your immediate attention, particularly shopping platforms, entertainment applications and social media accounts.

Keep essential notifications, such as important calls, work-related messages and family communications, enabled where necessary.

You can also use Focus Mode or Do Not Disturb settings while working, studying, reading or spending time with family. Reducing unnecessary interruptions makes it easier to stay engaged with the activity in front of you.

4. Stop scrolling without a purpose

Sometimes, we open social media without even realising why. We may be waiting for something, feeling bored or avoiding a task, and automatically reach for our phones.

This mindless behaviour makes it easier to lose track of time because there is no clear reason to stop scrolling.

Before opening an application, ask yourself a simple question: What am I looking for? Perhaps you want to reply to a message, check a particular update or watch a specific video. Once you have completed that activity, close the application instead of continuing to browse.

Another helpful technique is to avoid using social media as your default response to boredom. If you have a few free minutes, try taking a short walk, listening to a podcast, organising your workspace or simply allowing yourself to sit without looking at a screen.

The more intentional you become about using your phone, the easier it becomes to recognise when scrolling is no longer serving a purpose.

5. Curate your digital environment

The content you consume regularly can influence your thoughts, interests and overall online experience. If your social media feed is filled with negative news, unnecessary comparisons, arguments and emotionally exhausting content, spending time online can become overwhelming.

Take control of what appears on your feed. Unfollow accounts that encourage unhealthy comparisons, repeatedly share distressing content, or no longer align with your interests. Use options such as mute, unfollow and not interested to improve your recommendations.

Instead, follow accounts that provide educational information, practical advice, creative inspiration and meaningful discussions.

You can also organise your digital environment by removing applications you rarely use and keeping only the ones that genuinely serve a purpose.

Remember that you do not have to consume every update that appears on your screen. Being selective about what you watch, read and follow can make your online experience more positive and intentional.

3 Books to read instead of doomscrolling every day

6. Replace scrolling with activities that recharge you

Simply deciding to stop scrolling may not be enough if you do not have anything meaningful to replace the habit with. Many people return to their phones because scrolling has become their easiest source of entertainment whenever they have free time.

A more sustainable approach is to identify activities that can provide a similar sense of relaxation without requiring constant screen exposure.

For example, you could read a few pages of a book, spend time outdoors, write in a journal, practise a hobby, exercise or catch up with someone in person. Even small activities can help you become more comfortable spending time away from your phone.

You do not need to fill every free moment with productivity. Sometimes, sitting quietly, enjoying a cup of tea or taking a short break without checking notifications can be equally valuable.

The goal is to make your offline life engaging enough that you do not automatically turn to your phone whenever you have nothing to do.

7. Create a phone-free routine before bedtime

Late-night scrolling is one of the most common digital habits that can interfere with a healthy sleep routine. You may intend to watch one video before sleeping, but the endless stream of recommendations makes it difficult to put your phone down.

Using your phone close to bedtime can also expose you to stimulating content and make it harder to wind down.

Try establishing a phone-free period of at least 30 to 60 minutes before going to sleep. During this time, you can read, prepare for the next day, practise relaxation techniques or spend time with your family.

If you use your phone as an alarm, consider placing it away from your bed so that you are less tempted to keep checking it. You can also enable Do Not Disturb mode to avoid unnecessary interruptions.

A consistent bedtime routine can help you create a healthier relationship with technology while giving yourself an opportunity to disconnect from the constant flow of online information.

Final thoughts

A doom-scrolling detox does not mean abandoning social media or avoiding technology altogether. It means understanding that your attention is valuable and choosing where you want to invest it.

You do not have to follow all seven rules perfectly from the beginning. Start by changing one habit, such as avoiding your phone in the morning or setting a daily social media limit. Once that becomes easier, gradually introduce other boundaries. The internet will always have another video to watch, another update to check and another post to scroll through. But your time, energy and attention are limited.

Sometimes, the most productive thing you can do is put your phone down, step away from the screen and return to your own life.

item.title: 5 Life-changing lessons from It's Okay by Jaya Kishori
item.description: Discover 5 meaningful lessons from It's Okay by Jaya Kishori on accepting emotions, overcoming self-doubt, letting go and finding inner peace.
item.content:encoded:
Life rarely unfolds exactly as we imagine. Sometimes, despite our best efforts, things fall apart. Relationships change, plans fail, people disappoint us, and situations arise that leave us questioning ourselves.

In such moments, we often feel pressured to stay strong, hide our emotions and pretend that everything is fine. But what if we allowed ourselves to admit that things are not okay?

In It's Okay: A Book of Inspirational and Mystic Thoughts, Jaya Kishori offers a comforting perspective on dealing with life's challenges. Rather than encouraging readers to ignore their struggles, the book reminds them that problems, emotional setbacks and difficult experiences are natural parts of being human. It encourages readers to acknowledge their circumstances, develop a healthier perspective and find ways to move forward.

Drawing on personal experiences, spiritual teachings and stories passed down through generations, Jaya Kishori explores how people can approach life's uncertainties with greater understanding and emotional strength.

5 Life lessons from It's Okay by Jaya Kishori

1. Accepting your reality is the first step towards healing

One of the most important things we struggle with is accepting situations that do not go according to our expectations. We spend days questioning why something happened, wishing things had turned out differently or comparing our present circumstances with the life we once imagined.

However, constantly resisting reality does not change what has happened. It only makes it harder to find peace. The book encourages readers to understand that accepting a situation does not mean being happy about it or agreeing with everything that happened. It simply means acknowledging the truth instead of exhausting yourself by fighting something that is already beyond your control.

For instance, if you experience failure, lose an opportunity or go through a difficult phase in a relationship, accepting the situation allows you to understand what happened and decide what to do next.

The takeaway: You cannot always control what happens in life, but you can choose how you respond to it. Accepting reality gives you the clarity to stop dwelling on the past and start working towards a better future.

2. It is okay to acknowledge your emotions

Many people believe that being strong means never crying, feeling disappointed or expressing vulnerability. They hide their sadness behind smiles, tell everyone that they are fine and avoid discussing what is actually troubling them.

But ignoring emotions does not make them disappear. An important lesson to take from the book is that experiencing difficult emotions is a natural part of life. You do not have to feel happy every day, and you do not need to pretend that nothing affects you. Whether you are feeling lonely, anxious, disappointed or overwhelmed, acknowledging those emotions is an important step towards understanding yourself.

Instead of judging yourself for feeling a certain way, give yourself the space to understand what is causing those feelings. Sometimes, talking to someone you trust, taking a break or simply allowing yourself to process an experience can make a difference.

There is also a difference between acknowledging your emotions and allowing them to control your decisions. You can accept that you are hurt without letting that hurt define your entire life.

The takeaway: Emotional strength does not mean suppressing your feelings. It means understanding them, accepting them and learning how to deal with them more healthily.

3. Stop allowing other people's opinions to define you

We live in a world where people constantly have something to say about our choices, appearance, careers, relationships and personal lives. Sometimes, even a small comment from someone can make us question our abilities or feel inadequate.

Over time, we may start making decisions based on what others expect from us rather than what genuinely matters to us. This creates unnecessary pressure and takes away our ability to appreciate our own journey. The lesson here is to understand that everyone sees life through their own experiences, beliefs and expectations. What works for someone else may not necessarily work for you. Similarly, someone else's opinion about your life does not automatically make it the truth.

It is important to listen to constructive feedback, but there is no need to carry every criticism or allow every comment to affect your self-worth. You deserve to make decisions that align with your values and aspirations, even when everyone does not understand them.

The takeaway: Your worth should not depend on how others perceive you. Learn to value your own decisions, recognise your strengths and stop seeking approval from everyone around you.

4. Let go of what you cannot change

One of the biggest reasons people struggle to find peace is their attachment to things that are no longer within their control.

We revisit old conversations, regret decisions, think about missed opportunities and wonder what would have happened if we had chosen differently. While reflecting on the past can help us learn, constantly living in it prevents us from appreciating the present.

Letting go is not always easy, especially when something or someone has been an important part of your life. It takes time to accept certain endings, forgive yourself for past mistakes and make peace with experiences that did not turn out as expected.

However, holding on to every disappointment does not bring back what you have lost. Sometimes, moving forward requires accepting that certain chapters have ended.

This does not mean forgetting your experiences. It means taking the lessons from them without allowing them to become a permanent source of pain.

The takeaway: You cannot rewrite yesterday, but you can decide how you want to live tomorrow. Let go of unnecessary emotional baggage and give yourself the opportunity to experience life beyond your past.

5. Choose faith and a positive perspective during difficult times

Life can be unpredictable. There will be moments when you work hard but do not see results, when your plans fall apart or when you cannot understand why certain things are happening.

During such phases, it is easy to lose hope and believe that things will never improve. The book brings attention to the importance of spiritual understanding, faith and maintaining a positive outlook when dealing with life's challenges. Having faith does not mean expecting everything to happen exactly as you wish. Instead, it means developing the strength to face uncertainty without losing hope.

A positive perspective also does not require you to ignore your problems. It encourages you to look for possibilities, learn from difficult experiences and believe that your present circumstances do not have to determine your entire future.

For readers who find comfort in spirituality, prayer, reflection and faith can also become meaningful ways to navigate emotionally challenging periods.

The takeaway: Not every difficult experience will make sense immediately. Have faith, keep making sincere efforts and remind yourself that one challenging phase does not define your whole life.

Final thoughts

It's Okay by Jaya Kishori offers a reassuring reminder that life does not have to be perfect for us to find happiness and peace. We all experience difficult days, unexpected disappointments and moments when we feel lost. What matters is how we understand these experiences and allow ourselves to grow through them.

The five lessons from the book encourage us to accept reality, acknowledge our emotions, value ourselves, let go of the past and maintain faith during uncertain times.

Perhaps the most meaningful message is that saying "It's okay" should not become an excuse to ignore problems or tolerate situations that hurt us. Instead, it should give us the courage to acknowledge what is happening, face it honestly and take steps towards finding a solution.

Because sometimes, the first step towards changing your life is accepting that you do not have to have everything figured out right now.

item.title: Karnataka picks 8 startups for government projects worth nearly Rs 2 crore
item.description: Karnataka has picked eight startups to pilot solutions with government departments, with the Praja Seva Department and BWSSB committing projects worth nearly Rs 2 crore.
item.content:encoded:
Karnataka is looking to bring startups closer to the people who use public services.

The state government has selected eight startups under its Government First Initiative, allowing them to deploy their technology within government departments and address public sector challenges.

Announced on the opening day of the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) 2026 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC), the selection covers four startups each for the Praja Seva Department and the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB).

The two departments have a combined committed project value of nearly Rs 2 crore, inclusive of GST.

The initiative, launched by the Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology (IT & BT), Government of Karnataka, aims to make government departments potential customers for startups.

Rather than limiting innovation to demonstrations and proof-of-concept projects, the programme gives selected companies an opportunity to test market-ready solutions in real government environments.

Startups tackle citizen service challenges

The Praja Seva Department received 76 applications across four problem statements, covering AI-enabled grievance management, a unified citizen call centre, e-Office workflows and the availability of citizen-facing government IT services.

Four startups were selected, with a total committed project value of Rs 99.78 lakh, inclusive of GST.

SanMejora was selected for AI-enabled grievance management and redressal, while VTT AI Private Limited will work on the unified citizen call centre. Datafrontier Innovations Private Limited was chosen for the e-Office and officer workflow challenge, and Nife Apps Labs Pvt Ltd for ensuring the uptime of government IT services.

BWSSB received 74 applications across five challenge areas. These included reducing non-revenue water, planning treated wastewater reuse, intelligent asset management, GIS-enabled revenue and operational intelligence, and digital twins for integrated water management.

The selected startups are Smart Terra, UniaX Technologies, Krishi Hrudya Private Limited and Calypsion Innovations LLP. Each has been allocated Rs 25 lakh, taking the department's total committed project value to Rs 1 crore, inclusive of GST.

Selected startups could receive work orders of up to Rs 25 lakh

The programme allows selected startups to pilot, test and validate their solutions in partnership with the respective government departments. Subject to technical evaluation and programme guidelines, they will be eligible for direct work orders of up to Rs 25 lakh each.

The selection process involved five stages: application submission, eligibility screening, evaluation by the selection committee, discussions with officials from the respective departments, and final budget discussions.

Applications were invited between October 8 and October 23, 2026. Proposals were assessed on innovation, technical soundness, product readiness, relevance to government requirements, scalability and integration capabilities.

Speaking at the announcement, Shri Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home and Information Technology, Biotechnology and E-Governance, Government of Karnataka, said, "The Government First Initiative reflects our commitment to making government an active partner and customer of Karnataka's startup ecosystem.

We want to create opportunities for startups to take their innovations beyond the proof-of-concept stage and demonstrate their solutions in real-world governance settings."

He added that connecting startups with government departments could help translate homegrown innovation into measurable public impact and create opportunities for wider adoption.

Through the initiative, Karnataka aims to give startups a route to government procurement while helping public departments adopt technology-led solutions. The pilot deployments will also allow the government to assess how these products perform against actual administrative and infrastructure challenges.

item.title: Quick service restaurant chain Boba Bhai raises $18M in Series B round
item.description: Bubble tea and Korean street food brand Boba Bhai will use this funding round for store expansion and also launch new brands.
item.content:encoded:
Boba Bhai, an Indian bubble tea and Korean street food brand, has raised $18 million in a Series B funding round with participation from Left Lane Capital and BIG Capital, alongside existing investors including Titan Capital.

According to a statement, the round brings US-based Left Lane Capital on board as a new investor, while BIG Capital is increasing its investment in the company.

Boba Bhai will use this funding round for store expansion and also scale up new brands under Boba Bhai Ventures.

Boba Bhai had previously raised Rs 40 crore in March 2026 from 8i Ventures, Titan Capital Winners Fund and Global Growth Capital, BIG Capital and angel investors.

Founded in 2023, Boba Bhai has 120 stores across the country and serves more than three lakh orders every month which include physical and digital channels.

Boba Bhai founder Dhruv Kohli said, “Young Indian consumers are far more willing to experiment with global food formats today, but novelty alone does not build a lasting food brand. What matters is whether you can deliver the same product and experience consistently as you scale.”

He further noted the experience over the last three years will enable them to expand further and also create new brands.

Boba Bhai has built its growth around a combination of bubble tea, Korean street food and fusion offerings, catering to young Indian consumers who are increasingly experimenting with global flavours. The company has focused on product consistency, supply-chain discipline and store-level execution, while building its presence across physical retail, food-delivery platforms and quick commerce.

For the launch of new brands, this startup plans to use its existing capabilities across operations, supply chain, teams and digital distribution to launch and scale the concepts more efficiently.

Left Lane, the US-based consumer investment firm has backed food and consumer businesses across global markets including Blank Street Coffee and 7th Street Burger. Boba Bhai is the fourth company in India to be backed by Left Lane Capital.

“We have tracked Boba Bhai's growth for over two years and have been consistently impressed by how Dhruv has built the business. Boba Bhai stands out for its capital efficiency, its ability to quickly launch new concepts tuned to the local palate, and its relentless execution in delivering differentiated offerings for the Indian consumer,” said Arjun Kapur, Principal, Left Lane Capital.

item.title: 10 polite ways to set boundaries with family and colleagues
item.description: Discover 10 polite ways to set boundaries with family and colleagues while protecting your time, energy, personal space and emotional well-being.
item.content:encoded:
Setting boundaries is an important part of maintaining healthy relationships, but it is not always easy. Saying no to a family member, declining an extra task at work or asking someone to respect your personal space can sometimes feel uncomfortable. Many people worry that setting boundaries will make them appear rude, selfish or uncooperative.

However, boundaries are not about pushing people away. They help establish mutual respect and make relationships more balanced. Whether you are dealing with family expectations or workplace demands, learning to communicate your limits calmly can protect your time, energy and well-being.

Here are 10 polite ways to set boundaries without creating unnecessary conflict.

1. Say no without giving lengthy explanations

You do not have to justify every decision with a detailed explanation. If a family member asks you to attend an event or a colleague requests help when you are already busy, you can politely decline.

Try saying, "Thank you for asking, but I won't be able to manage it this time." A short and respectful response communicates your decision without making the conversation unnecessarily complicated.

Also Read
7 Powerful Nonfiction Books to Set Boundaries Without Guilt

2. Be clear about your availability

Constant calls, messages and last-minute requests can make it difficult to protect your personal time. Let people know when you are available and when you need to focus on other responsibilities.

For example, you could tell a colleague, "I usually respond to work messages during office hours. I'll get back to you tomorrow morning." Similarly, let family members know when you need uninterrupted time for work, studies or rest.

3. Avoid taking responsibility for everyone's emotions

It is natural to care about how others feel, but you cannot make every person happy all the time. Sometimes, people may feel disappointed when you decline a request or express a different opinion.

Instead of changing your decision out of guilt, acknowledge their feelings while maintaining your position. You can say, "I understand that this is important to you, but I still need to make the decision that works for me."

4. Keep work and personal life separate

Workplace communication can easily extend beyond office hours, especially when colleagues expect immediate responses. However, being responsible at work does not mean being available around the clock.

Politely communicate your working hours and avoid responding to non-urgent requests during your personal time. You can say, "I'd be happy to discuss this during working hours tomorrow." This creates a professional boundary without sounding unhelpful.

5. Speak up when someone makes uncomfortable comments

Family gatherings and workplace conversations sometimes involve personal remarks about appearance, relationships, salary or lifestyle choices. Even when people claim they are joking, repeated comments can become uncomfortable.

Instead of ignoring your feelings, communicate your discomfort calmly. Try saying, "I know you may not mean it negatively, but I'd prefer not to discuss this topic." Being respectful does not mean you have to accept every comment.

6. Stop agreeing to tasks beyond your capacity

Taking on every responsibility may make you seem dependable, but it can eventually lead to stress and exhaustion. Before accepting an additional task, consider your existing commitments and available time.

At work, you can say, "I can take this up, but I'll need to revisit the timeline for my current tasks." With family, try saying, "I would like to help, but I already have a few responsibilities to manage today." This communicates your limits while keeping the conversation constructive.

7. Ask for privacy and personal space

Healthy relationships also require respect for individual privacy. Family members may sometimes expect access to personal conversations, belongings or decisions, while colleagues may ask questions that feel too personal.

You can politely communicate what you are comfortable sharing. For example, say, "I'd prefer to keep that matter private" or "I need some time to myself right now." You can value your relationships while maintaining personal space.

8. Avoid discussing sensitive topics when you are uncomfortable

Not every conversation needs to happen immediately. If someone brings up a sensitive subject when you are tired, upset or unprepared, it is reasonable to ask for another time.

Try saying, "I'd rather discuss this when we both have more time" or "I'm not comfortable talking about this right now." This helps prevent emotionally charged conversations and gives everyone an opportunity to communicate more thoughtfully.

9. Be consistent with the boundaries you establish

Setting a boundary once may not be enough if people are used to you always agreeing. They may need time to understand that your response has changed.

For instance, if you have communicated that you cannot take work calls after office hours, try not to repeatedly make exceptions for non-urgent matters. Consistency helps others understand your expectations and reduces confusion over time.

10. Communicate your expectations before problems arise

Boundaries are easier to maintain when people understand your expectations early. Rather than waiting until you feel overwhelmed, have open conversations about your availability, responsibilities and personal preferences.

You might tell your family that you need a specific period for uninterrupted study or let your colleagues know how much time you need to complete an assignment. Clear communication can prevent misunderstandings and make everyday interactions smoother.

Final thoughts

Setting boundaries with family and colleagues does not mean being distant, unkind or difficult to work with. It means understanding your limits and communicating them in a respectful way.

You may not always receive an immediate positive response, and some people may need time to adjust. However, you do not have to abandon your needs simply to avoid disappointing others.

Start with small changes, use calm language and remain consistent. Healthy boundaries allow you to maintain meaningful relationships while making enough room for your own priorities, personal space and well-being.

item.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 18, 2026)
item.description: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here’s the roundup for Wednesday, November 18, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
From the Nvidia chair ruling out plans to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO to GTA 6’s arrival for Indian players, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.

Latest news

Nvidia chair says no plan to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO

Nvidia’s board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, chair Harvey Jones said on the chipmaker’s earnings call on Wednesday. His remarks came hours after the co-founder said he would be honoured to return if the board decided it was in the company's best interest.

The board’s decision effectively closes the door on an immediate return for Huang, whose resignation has raised questions about corporate governance, national security, and the future leadership of one of the world’s most valuable technology companies. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and spent more than three decades transforming it from a graphics-chip manufacturer into a dominant supplier of computing infrastructure for artificial intelligence (AI).

Read more

GTA 6 is here: Everything Indian players need to know

Grand Theft Auto VI goes live on Thursday, 19 November 2026, more than 13 years after GTA V. Store listings in India show a 12:00 am IST start. The game arrives on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X and S only. There is no PC version, and none for the PS4 or Xbox One.

PlayStation India lists the Standard Edition at Rs 5,999 and the Ultimate Edition at Rs 7,499. Both come with the Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+, Rockstar's subscription service. The Ultimate Edition adds an upgrade pack, and buyers of the Standard Edition can reportedly move up later for Rs 1,500, so there is no need to decide in a hurry.

Read more

Funding news

Botsync raises $11M to expand industrial automation

Singapore-headquartered Botsync has raised $11 million in a round led by IvyCap Ventures, a homegrown venture capital firm. 

Other participants include Capital 2B, a deeptech investor; Taiwan-based accelerator and venture investor AppWorks; South-East Asian early-stage investor Iterative; Singapore angel network AngelCentral; Genesis Alternate Investments; and angel investor Nalin Advani. 

The round follows a January 2026 Series A extension led by SGInnovate, taking total funding above $20 million.

Read more

Fatehpuria Hygiene secures Rs 100 Cr in first equity fundraise

Fatehpuria Hygiene, a trading, supply chain and fulfilment company, has raised Rs 100 crore in its first equity fundraise, led by investor Madhu Kela.

The company said it plans to use the capital to strengthen its nationwide presence and build a technology-driven supply chain ecosystem. It aims to expand into more than 50 major cities over the next 24 months and develop an AI-enabled, integrated supply chain network.

Read more

CountAI raises Rs 10 Cr in seed funding led by Equirus InnovateX Fund

Coimbatore-based industrial AI startup CountAI has raised Rs 10 crore in seed funding led by Equirus InnovateX Fund to expand product development and manufacturing applications. Founded by Harshavardhan Thirupathi and Venkataramanan, the company develops AI-powered quality control and automation systems. Its flagship product, Knit-I, detects fabric defects in real time on circular knitting machines and triggers stoppages to reduce waste. 

The technology is deployed across manufacturers including Aarti International, KPR and Indorama. CountAI reports an 80% reduction in defect-related losses across more than 62 machines at Aarti International, while a deployment in Uzbekistan reduced knitting waste from 1.5% to 0.2%. The company plans to expand into other industrial quality control applications.

Finvolve backs Soket AI Labs in seed round to develop indigenous foundation models

Venture capital fund Finvolve and India Accelerator have invested an undisclosed amount in Bengaluru-based Soket AI Labs as part of its seed funding round, co-led by Bajaj Finance, Pennant Technologies and the IndiaAI Mission. Soket AI is developing indigenous foundation models for mathematics, coding, reasoning and multilingual applications under Project EKA. Its recently launched EKA-1 is a 26-billion-parameter model. 

The company is also building an integrated AI stack covering foundation models, agentic systems and inference infrastructure. The funding will support research, technology development and sovereign AI solutions for enterprise and mission-critical sectors, including banking, financial services, cybersecurity and defence. Soket aims to enable organisations to deploy AI within their own infrastructure, addressing data sovereignty, security and transparency requirements.

Other news

IndoSpace invests Rs 350 Cr to develop 1.05M sq. ft. industrial park in Karnataka

IndoSpace has launched Narasapura-II, a 1.05 million sq. ft. industrial and logistics park in Karnataka, backed by an investment of Rs 350 crore. Located in the KIADB-notified Narasapura Industrial Area in Kolar district, the development builds on the company's existing 1.60 million sq. ft. Narasapura-I facility. The park will serve businesses across manufacturing, e-commerce, warehousing, engineering and third-party logistics.

It offers connectivity to NH 75 and NH 48, Bengaluru's key consumption centres and nearby industrial clusters. Facilities include digital access systems, IoT-enabled infrastructure monitoring, AI-based utility management and a 24x7 integrated command centre. IndoSpace said the development will strengthen its presence in Karnataka's industrial and logistics market.

Neysa deploys 8,192 AMD Instinct MI350X GPUs to expand AI computing capacity in India

AI cloud provider Neysa has deployed an 8,192-GPU AMD Instinct MI350X cluster on its Tytan bare-metal AI infrastructure platform in Mumbai. The operational deployment will support AI model training, fine-tuning, generative AI and large-scale inference workloads. Global customers have already contracted the capacity for AI deployments in India. The cluster uses AMD EPYC processors and the ROCm software ecosystem, offering configurations through bare metal, Slurm and Kubernetes.

The deployment expands Neysa's silicon-agnostic infrastructure strategy, allowing customers to choose accelerator architecture, networking, storage and operating environments according to their requirements. The partnership with AMD aims to increase access to dedicated, high-density AI computing infrastructure for Indian enterprises and global customers.

The ePlane Company selects LYNX MOSA.ic software platform for e200X electric aircraft

The ePlane Company has selected Lynx’s LYNX MOSA.ic platform to manage mixed-criticality software on its e200X electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft. The three-seat aircraft is designed for air ambulance, urban cargo and passenger services. The platform will allow flight-critical systems, including vehicle and energy management, to operate in isolated software partitions alongside lower-criticality functions such as sensor processing and situational awareness.

Built around a separation kernel-based hypervisor, LYNX MOSA.ic supports shared computing while maintaining safety and cybersecurity isolation. The platform is certifiable to DO-178C Design Assurance Level A, enabling the ePlane Company to develop modular aircraft functions while keeping flight-critical software isolated.

IIT Kanpur, Bharat1.ai launch AI Kavach cybersecurity lab for financial AI systems

IIT Kanpur’s Wadhwani School of AI and Intelligent Systems and Bharat1.ai have launched AI Kavach, an AI cybersecurity and assurance lab focused on banking, payments, lending, insurance and digital financial services. The lab will conduct adversarial testing of financial AI systems, develop containment and sandboxing technologies for autonomous AI agents, and research AI assurance, traceability and vulnerability disclosure.

It will also support workforce development through fellowships, security exercises and industry programmes targeting over 300 students and professionals annually. The initiative will use computing resources supported by the IndiaAI Mission. The partners aim to build shared security evaluation frameworks and connect financial institutions, fintech companies, researchers, regulators and cybersecurity experts to improve the safety of AI deployment.

Exotel appoints Kamolika Peres, Samaresh Parida as independent directors

AI-powered customer experience platform Exotel has appointed Kamolika Peres and Samaresh Parida as independent directors to strengthen its board as it expands across India and international markets. Peres brings over two decades of enterprise technology experience, having held senior roles at Autodesk, ServiceNow, Google Cloud, SAP, IBM and Ericsson.

Parida, a Chartered Accountant and IIM Ahmedabad alumnus, has over 30 years of experience across telecommunications, finance and corporate governance. He previously held leadership positions at Vodafone and PepsiCo and served as an independent director and Audit Committee chairman at IDBI Bank. Their appointments will support Exotel's strategic planning, financial oversight, risk management and corporate governance as it scales its AI-led customer experience platform.

Hitachi Systems India opens Bengaluru cybersecurity centre and partners with CrowdStrike

Hitachi Systems India has launched an Advanced Global Delivery Centre in Bengaluru and partnered with CrowdStrike to provide AI-powered cybersecurity and managed security services across India, Asia Pacific and the Middle East. The collaboration will use CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform to secure endpoints, identity, cloud, data and AI systems. Hitachi Systems India will also participate in Project QuiltWorks, helping organisations identify and address vulnerabilities exposed by frontier AI models through AI-powered scanning and remediation services.

The partnership includes Falcon Next-Gen SIEM services to modernise security operations and support the transition to AI-driven security operations centres. The centre will help enterprises secure AI adoption, address emerging cyber threats and strengthen security infrastructure. Hitachi Systems India has over 2,800 employees and serves more than 1,000 customers.

Sunfox Technologies appoints Subrata Mazumdar as VP of Strategy and Growth

Dehradun-based medtech company Sunfox Technologies has appointed Subrata Mazumdar as Vice President of Strategy and Growth. Based in Mumbai, he will lead market expansion, portfolio strategy, go-to-market planning, pricing and strategic partnerships. Mazumdar brings over 30 years of commercial leadership experience across Abbott, Sanofi, Novartis, Claris Lifesciences and Wockhardt.

During his 15-year tenure at Abbott Diabetes Care, he led the launch of FreeStyle Libre and Libre Pro, helping establish India's continuous glucose monitoring market. The appointment follows Sunfox's $7 million Series A funding round. The company develops Spandan, a portable ECG platform, and plans to expand its reach across homes, clinics and healthcare systems in India and international markets.

Clarissa Group launches farm-to-home and FMCG platform Clarissa Fresh

Clarissa Group has launched Clarissa Fresh, a farm-to-home and FMCG platform offering fresh fruits, vegetables, daily essentials and curated gifting solutions. The move marks the group's expansion beyond hospitality and real estate into agriculture and fresh produce. The platform sources products from its farms in Mukteshwar and Jim Corbett, which grow apples, kiwis, dragon fruit, mulberries and exotic mango varieties, alongside trusted partner farms.

Its primary focus will be B2B customers, including hotels, hospitality businesses, corporate offices and institutional buyers, while also serving individual consumers. Clarissa Fresh plans to expand distribution through quick-commerce and e-commerce platforms such as Blinkit, Instamart and BigBasket. The company also plans to introduce technology-driven sourcing, traceability and ordering systems to support consistent quality and timely deliveries.

Even Hospitals launches public dashboard tracking clinical outcomes and hospital performance

Even Hospitals has launched Even Spotlight, a public-facing dashboard that provides daily updates on clinical outcomes, patient experience and hospital operations. Each metric is displayed against a defined target or benchmark, with a traffic-light system indicating performance levels. Powered by the hospital's in-house operating system, the dashboard currently covers outpatient and inpatient services, with additional measures planned.

It also maintains a public changelog documenting changes or withdrawals of metrics and preserves historical data when measurement definitions change. The initiative aims to improve transparency and accountability by giving patients access to hospital performance data. The launch follows Even Healthcare's $50 million Series B funding round led by Khosla Ventures.

LinkedIn, Wadhwani AI launch programme to train 2,000 entrepreneurs in Northeast India

LinkedIn and Wadhwani AI have signed an MoU to launch AI for Future SMEs, a 12-month programme aimed at building AI and digital skills among 2,000 small and micro entrepreneurs across Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Meghalaya and Manipur. Developed in collaboration with state governments and district councils, the initiative will offer mobile-first training, mentorship and joint certification.

The curriculum will cover AI fundamentals, generative AI, prompt engineering, responsible AI, digital safety and practical business applications, including marketing, customer communication, inventory management and market research. Training will be tailored to local industries such as handloom, handicrafts, bamboo, tourism, food processing and agriculture. The programme will use open-source AI tools and offline learning resources for areas with limited connectivity, with assessments to track improvements in digital skills and business adoption.

SiMa.ai launches Palette 3.0 to boost Physical AI performance by up to 3.5x

SiMa.ai has launched Palette 3.0, a software release designed to improve the performance and efficiency of Physical AI applications across robotics and autonomous drones. The platform enables concurrent execution of multiple AI models on its Modalix MLSoC, supporting workloads such as large language models and vision-language models within tight power and memory limits.

It uses speculative decoding algorithms, including EAGLE3, DFlash and Gemma 4 MTP, to increase model processing speed by up to 3.5x. Palette 3.0 also supports large Mixture-of-Experts models, including GPT-OSS-20B, on a 16GB module. SiMa.ai has released open-source capabilities, documentation and a Model Browser for developers.

ANSR launches 500Leaders platform to develop GCC leadership talent

ANSR has launched 500Leaders, a dedicated platform aimed at identifying, developing and connecting senior leadership talent with Global Capability Centres (GCCs). The platform will focus on three pillars: leadership opportunities, learning and community. It will offer executives access to leadership roles across GCCs, development programmes, mentorship and an invitation-only peer network through the ANSR Leadership Forum.

The initiative seeks to address the growing demand for leaders capable of driving enterprise-wide transformation, innovation and AI adoption as GCCs evolve into strategic business centres. ANSR said it had helped place more than 2,500 leaders across the GCC ecosystem over the past year. The launch follows its partnership with the Indian School of Business to introduce the LATITUDe executive education programme for GCC leaders.

Autodesk, Neilsoft to establish Digital Twin innovation centre in Pune

Autodesk and Neilsoft have partnered to establish a Centre of Excellence (COE) for Building Information Modelling (BIM) and Digital Twin technologies in Pune. The facility, located at Neilsoft's headquarters, will focus on accelerating digital transformation across the Architecture, Engineering, Construction and Operations (AECO) industry.

The centre will combine Autodesk's Forma platform and Tandem technologies with Neilsoft's engineering expertise to develop solutions for building operations, integrated design and construction, sustainability and software engineering. It will also demonstrate a live Digital Twin of Neilsoft's 10-storey, three-acre office complex. The partnership aims to support the adoption of AI-powered energy optimisation, predictive maintenance and data-driven building management solutions across India and international markets.

HyugaLife onboards Tata 1mg's health supplement portfolio

Health and wellness e-commerce platform HyugaLife has onboarded Tata 1mg's range of health supplements, expanding its product portfolio. The offering includes whey and plant-based protein powders, creatine, omega-3 fish oil, probiotics and other nutritional supplements.

The collaboration aims to improve consumer access to verified health and wellness products amid growing interest in preventive healthcare and nutritional supplementation. HyugaLife said the partnership would strengthen its product offerings and provide consumers with a wider selection of established healthcare brands.

Monedo Financial Services crosses Rs 1,000 crore asset mark

Monedo Financial Services has crossed Rs 1,000 crore in total assets, triggering its transition from the Base Layer to the Middle Layer under the Reserve Bank of India's Scale-Based Regulation framework for non-banking financial companies (NBFCs).

The transition brings additional regulatory requirements covering corporate governance, risk management, capital adequacy and financial disclosures. The Mumbai-based NBFC said it had strengthened its board oversight, compliance and internal audit functions in preparation for the change.

Monedo's assets crossed Rs 1,000 crore on November 12, 2026, having grown more than sixfold over three years. The company is targeting assets under management of ₹1,400-1,500 crore in FY27 and aims to reach ₹5,000 crore within two years. Its focus areas include supply chain finance, SME lending and healthcare financing.

Believe partners Hoopr Smash to offer music catalogues for brand campaigns

Global artist development company Believe has partnered with Hoopr Smash to make its Indian music catalogues available for commercial licensing by brands, agencies and content creators. The partnership will provide access to music from labels including Think Music, Ishtar and Believe's Artist Services portfolio.

Hoopr Smash currently serves more than 135 brands and offers over 20,000 pre-cleared tracks. The partnership aims to expand licensed music usage and create additional revenue opportunities for artists and labels.

Syncro1 launches AI-powered digital talent recruitment platform

Syncro1, an AI-powered digital Talent Partner platform, has launched with the aim of transforming recruitment through technology-led hiring and outcome-based commercial models. The platform connects organisations with a network of independent recruitment professionals through structured hiring workflows.

Its eight-layer AI-powered candidate screening system evaluates profiles across multiple parameters, moving beyond conventional keyword matching. The platform also incorporates a three-layer information consent framework to improve transparency and ensure responsible sharing of candidate data.

item.title: Apollo, Microsoft turn to AI to help hospitals learn from medical errors
item.description: The partnership aims to turn fragmented hospital records into faster incident reviews and shared lessons.
item.content:encoded:
An artificial intelligence system developed by Apollo Hospitals with Microsoft is being used to speed up reviews of patient falls, medication errors and readmissions. Apollo said the system has coincided with fewer recorded incidents, although the evidence published so far does not establish that AI itself has reduced patient harm.

Apollo and Microsoft developed a Daily Tiered Huddle agent to support clinical-governance teams. It brings together hospital records, flags cases, builds patient timelines and prompts clinicians for missing details. It also suggests assessments for doctors to check and amend. The tool is in production at some Apollo hospitals.

“For anyone to process 600 cases per month with incomplete data and come up with a meaningful decision is difficult,” said Dr Rohini Sridhar, Apollo’s chief of medical services. The agent is intended to reduce the time spent assembling records, leaving clinicians more time to investigate complex cases.

Apollo said more than 60% of cases reviewed by its huddles were closed within three days in November 2026. It also noted fewer falls and medication errors in July-September than in the same quarter of 2025. Dr Sridhar said staff satisfaction with error handling improved by almost 30%, based on the hospital’s annual safety-culture survey.

These are hospital-reported results published in a Microsoft case study. The account does not provide incident counts, patient-volume-adjusted rates or an independent assessment.

The system is also designed to identify patterns across departments, although Apollo said this analysis is still being developed. It flagged a cluster of central-line-associated bloodstream infections in a bone marrow transplant unit. Juliet Joji Varghese, Apollo’s director of nursing in Chennai, said the system helps staff learn from incidents elsewhere in the network.

Beyond the Apollo and Microsoft push, there are other initiatives that reflect the expanding use of AI in routine healthcare operations and diagnostics.

In April, AstraZeneca and the Telangana government agreed to introduce Qure.ai’s AI-supported chest X-ray screening in 20 public health facilities. The technology is intended to flag high-risk lung nodules for further assessment. Manipal Hospitals has also worked with Google Cloud on a generative AI tool for nurse handovers, which Google said had been rolled out across 23 hospitals by July 2025. 

India is also beginning to establish a framework for responsible adoption. The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, launched in 2021, laid the foundation for interoperable digital health records. In February 2026, the Centre launched the Strategy for AI in Healthcare for India, and the Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI (BODH). 

Developed with IIT Kanpur and the National Health Authority, BODH is intended to evaluate AI models using diverse health data while protecting patient records.

The World Health Organization, in a July 2026 report, highlighted ethical and oversight challenges arising from AI in health research, including risks that existing review systems may not adequately address.
