item.title: Paytm public-market investors earn 1.7x returns in five years as shares hit record high
item.description: An analysis of the company's shareholder base shows that public investors have collectively acquired around 41.5 crore shares at a weighted average price of Rs 1,092 apiece.
item.content:encoded:
Public shareholders in One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, have earned returns of approximately 1.7 times their investment over the past five years, as the fintech company's shares climbed to a new high, reflecting a significant expansion in public ownership and institutional participation since its stock market debut.

An analysis of the company's shareholder base shows that public investors have collectively acquired around 41.5 crore shares at a weighted average price of Rs 1,092 apiece. Based on the National Stock Exchange's closing price of Rs 1,903 on November 17, 2026, this translates into an annualised return of approximately 17%.

The stock closed at Rs 1,888.30 on Wednesday.

The calculation includes both investors who subscribed to Paytm's initial public offering (IPO) in November 2021 and those who subsequently purchased shares from pre-IPO shareholders in the secondary market.

However, investors who received shares in the IPO at Rs 2,150 apiece are still trading at approximately 0.9 times their initial investment, underscoring the difference between returns for the original IPO allotment cohort and those for public-market investors who entered at lower prices.

The analysis, based on NSE and BSE block deals, bulk deals and disclosed open-market transactions, also shows that pre-IPO shareholders have sold approximately 34.6 crore shares since listing at a weighted average price of Rs 832 apiece.

At the November 17 closing price, these shares are valued at around 2.3 times their average selling price, translating into an annualised return of approximately 40.4% for investors who acquired them at the reported average price.

Paytm's shareholder composition has undergone a significant shift since its market debut, with the company's free float increasing from around 15% at listing in 2021 to approximately 68%.

Domestic institutional ownership has also risen substantially, increasing from 1.3% in September 2022 to 29.5% in September 2026.

Mutual funds now hold around 21.2% of the company's equity, while insurance companies account for another 6.2%, indicating a larger institutional presence in its shareholder base.

The increase in institutional participation comes as Paytm has worked through regulatory and business challenges while focusing on its core payments operations, merchant ecosystem and financial services distribution.

Under founder and Chief Executive Vijay Shekhar Sharma, the company has continued to invest in technology, expand its merchant network and strengthen its financial services offerings, alongside efforts to improve operational efficiency and build a more sustainable business model.

Paytm's operating performance has also improved, with the company reporting six consecutive quarters of profitability.

For the second quarter of FY27, the company reported revenue of Rs 2,648 crore, up 28% year-on-year, while EBITDA increased 90% to Rs 270 crore. Its EBITDA margin reached 10% for the first time, while profit after tax stood at Rs 225 crore.

The improvement in financial performance reflects higher operating leverage and the company's continued focus on profitable growth, as it seeks to strengthen its position in India's digital payments and financial services market.

The expansion in domestic institutional ownership and the rise in public shareholding mark a significant change in Paytm's investor profile since its listing.

item.title: GTA 6 is here: Everything Indian players need to know
item.description: The biggest game launch in years arrives on 19 November. Here is what it costs in India, what you need to play it, and what is still unclear.
item.content:encoded:
Grand Theft Auto VI goes live on Thursday, 19 November 2026, more than 13 years after GTA V. Store listings in India show a 12:00 am IST start. The game arrives on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X and S only. There is no PC version, and none for the PS4 or Xbox One.

The price in rupees

PlayStation India lists the Standard Edition at Rs 5,999 and the Ultimate Edition at Rs 7,499. Both come with the Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+, Rockstar's subscription service. The Ultimate Edition adds an upgrade pack, and buyers of the Standard Edition can reportedly move up later for Rs 1,500, so there is no need to decide in a hurry.

For anyone who already owns a console, that is the whole bill. For everyone else, the game is the small part of the cost. Amazon India listed the PS5 Slim Digital at Rs 64,990 and the Disc model at Rs 69,985 on 28 October. Add the Standard Edition and a new buyer pays about Rs 70,989 on the digital console. Prices move, so check the final checkout figure before buying.

Do not pay extra for the disc drive

There is one trap for new buyers. The boxed version of GTA 6 reportedly contains only a download code, not a game disc. So the Rs 4,995 extra for the disc-drive PS5 buys you nothing for this game at launch. It may still make sense for other games or for resale, but if GTA 6 is the reason you are buying, the digital console is the cheaper route.

Blinkit will deliver it in minutes

Indian players do not have to wait for a courier. Quick-commerce platform Blinkit announced on its official account that GTA 6 is now available on its app, with delivery in minutes. It is live in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata and Ahmedabad, and Blinkit says more cities will follow over the next day.

What arrives is a physical box with a download code inside, which matches the disc-free boxes described above. Blinkit pitched the box as a collectible for the shelf. Buyers can redeem the code and start downloading at once, so the game is ready to play when it unlocks on 19 November. Blinkit's post ended with a joke that it expects a suspicious number of people to take sick leave in the next few days.

Get the download done early

Pre-loading opened on 12 November. On the PS5, the game needs at least 212 GB of free space, according to PlayStation's store page. That is a long download on a slow connection and a big bite out of a standard broadband data cap, so it is worth checking both. Players on the Xbox Series S, which has less storage, should clear space first.

The free month that costs money later

Eligible digital pre-orders include one free month of GTA+. PlayStation India says the offer needs a digital pre-order before 20 November and must be claimed by 31 March 2027. After that month, GTA+ becomes a paid plan that renews automatically unless you cancel. Set a reminder if you do not want to keep paying.

What the game is about

The story follows two lead characters, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Rockstar Games describes a criminal conspiracy that spreads across the state of Leonida after a bank job goes wrong. Leonida is a fictional take on Florida, and it includes a modern Vice City, a place longtime fans will know from the series' past. It is the first numbered GTA with a female lead, and the two characters can work together or split up. Reports suggest the map is roughly twice the size of GTA V's, though Rockstar has not given an official figure.

The game is single-player at launch. In the US it carries a Mature 17+ rating from the ESRB, so this is not a game for children, and Indian parents buying it as a gift should keep that in mind.

What is still missing

Rockstar has not announced a PC version. That matters in India, where many serious gamers play on PCs and gaming laptops because consoles are expensive. A gaming laptop will not help on launch day. Rockstar has also not confirmed a date for GTA Online, the multiplayer side of the series.

Reports point to a PC release in the first quarter of 2027, but that is a rumour and Rockstar has not confirmed it. For Indian players with a capable gaming PC, the choice is between playing now on a console and waiting a few months. For those who do not own a console, waiting could save close to Rs 65,000.

Consoles are selling out

Demand for consoles has jumped since Rockstar's extended gameplay look appeared on Netflix. Reports from other countries say resellers have bought up stock and are charging nearly double the usual price for the PS5 Pro and the Xbox Series S, with many listings sold out.

It is not yet clear how far this has reached India, and the figures quoted for Indian listings are not reliable. Still, a buyer who needs a console for launch day should expect tight stock. Buy from authorised sellers, compare the final checkout price, and treat any listing far above the price Sony or Microsoft lists with suspicion.

Why India is watching

The console barrier is the story here. At about Rs 65,000 for the cheapest PS5, the machine costs ten times as much as the game. GTA 6 may push a number of Indian buyers into their first console, but it also shows how far the console market still has to travel in a country where most people play on phones. Whether this launch widens that market, or simply sells to those who already own a console, is the question to watch in the weeks ahead.

Prices and times are as listed by PlayStation India and retailers in early November.

item.title: Sarvam’s move to host Chinese AI models triggers debate
item.description: Sarvam’s decision to host Chinese AI models on Indian infrastructure has ignited a debate over AI sovereignty, public funding and India's ambitions to develop homegrown frontier technology.
item.content:encoded:
Sarvam AI’s decision to host Chinese-developed artificial intelligence models on its India-based infrastructure has reopened questions about what it means to build sovereign AI. 

With its newly-launched Token Factory offering access to models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Z.ai, alongside its own models and Google’s Gemma, the Bengaluru-based company is positioning itself as an AI developer and an inference provider. 

The move has attracted criticism from those who believe a company backed by public resources should prioritise original Indian research, as well as support from those who see a commercial opportunity in hosting international models locally.

Announcing the service, Sarvam said, “We host our own models, and the full range of best-in-class open-weight models, in India.” It added that enterprises would have more models to choose from and “an AI stack they can own without lock-ins”.

Token Factory is an inference platform, which provides the computing infrastructure required to run trained AI models and generate responses. Instead of purchasing expensive hardware and managing individual models themselves, developers can access several models through a single application programming interface. 

Sarvam said its customised software and infrastructure allow it to compete on speed, reliability and cost.

The debate

The criticism centres on the distinction between hosting AI and developing it. Sanchit Monga, chief executive of Runanywhere AI, a Y Combinator-backed AI infrastructure company, questioned whether the launch reflected the ambitions associated with Sarvam’s selection under the government’s IndiaAI Mission. He wrote, “I wanted Sarvam to be the lab that ships frontier research out of India. After that much capital and subsidized compute, this is not it.”

Similar concerns were expressed by technology commentator Shakthi, who argued that hosting predominantly Chinese models was not what the country’s sovereign AI ambitions should amount to.

The debate became particularly interesting after Sarvam co-founder Vivek Raghavan’s remarks at the Bengaluru Tech Summit on November 17. 

Warning against India’s dependence on foreign AI systems, he said, “A lot of people are proud to say that India is the largest user of ChatGPT. But that is not a good thing. We are exporting data and importing intelligence.” 

Although he was not directly addressing Token Factory, his comments underline the strategic concerns surrounding dependence on foreign-developed models.

There are, however, strong commercial arguments for Sarvam’s approach. Hemant Mohapatra, a partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the launch, pointing out that international inference providers are already making money by hosting foreign models in India. He argued that there was considerable demand for such services, particularly as computing capacity becomes increasingly difficult to secure in some markets.

Technology entrepreneur Nikhil Pahwa also defended the company’s need to develop a sustainable business. “They’re a business, and they have to work in shareholder interest. Nationalism is a pitch that got them the GPUs. They’re not expected to deliver anything beyond their contract,” he wrote.

Nischal Jain, co-founder of Egma AI, offered a more nuanced assessment. While acknowledging that companies must generate revenue, he argued that Sarvam had acquired a particular significance in India’s technology ecosystem. “Sarvam was supposed to be India’s answer to the US & China. When we don’t see their frontier labs do these kinda things, it looks demotivating in an already tough situation. Everyone's gotta make money and I empathise with both ends of arguments,” he wrote.

Questions have also emerged around the platform’s competitiveness. Atharva Ingle, an AI engineer at competing inference provider JarvisLabs, said his company had compared the performance of three models across the two platforms. “We’re on par with or faster than Sarvam across speed and latency metrics, while offering lower pricing,” he claimed.

Reduce AI dependence

The wider context is India’s attempt to reduce dependence on overseas AI technology. 

The IndiaAI Mission, approved in March 2024 with an outlay of approximately Rs 10,372 crore, is intended to strengthen domestic computing infrastructure, research and foundational model development. 

Sarvam was selected in 2025 for indigenous model development and received subsidised access to 4,096 Nvidia H100 GPUs. The reported subsidy was Rs 98.68 crore. The company also raised over $300 million at a reported valuation of $1.5 billion.

Ultimately, hosting foreign models on Indian infrastructure and developing indigenous models are different achievements, although they need not be mutually exclusive. Local hosting can improve data residency, access and computing efficiency, while a successful inference business could generate revenue to support further research. 

The more important test will be whether Sarvam can translate its public support and commercial expansion into original technology and competitive Indian models.

item.title: Kotak MF, BlackRock among investors buying Rs 1,905-Cr stake in Groww
item.description: The investors collectively purchased 8.70 crore equity shares, representing a 1.38% stake in Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of Groww, at an average price of Rs 219 apiece on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Domestic and global institutional investors such as Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund and BlackRock, have increased their stake in Groww by acquiring shares worth Rs 1,905 crore, according to block deal data on NSE.

The investors collectively purchased 8.70 crore equity shares, representing a 1.38% stake in Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of Groww, at an average price of Rs 219 apiece on Tuesday.

Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund (MF) led the buying spree, acquiring 2.05 crore shares or a 0.33% stake, for Rs 448.95 crore, making it the biggest buyer in the transaction.

The share purchase increased Kotak MF's stake in Groww to 2.21% from 1.89%.

BlackRock, the world's largest asset management company, was the second-largest buyer of Bengaluru-based Groww, picking up more than 1.34 crore shares for Rs 294.55 crore.

Other domestic institutional investors participating in the transaction included Tata Mutual Fund, National Pension System (NPS) Trust, and HDFC Life Insurance.

The overseas buyers included Societe Generale, BNP Paribas, Fidelity Investments, Viridian Asset Management, Susquehanna International Group, Canada's RBC Global Asset Management, Swiss banking major UBS, Morgan Stanley, and Ghisallo Capital Management.

London-based Investment management firm Redwheel, Australia's largest superannuation fund Rest Super, Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois and Norway's Government Pension Fund Global were also among the buyers.

On the selling side of the deal, US-based venture capital firm Ribbit Capital, through two of its affiliates, offloaded 8.70 crore equity shares at the same price, as per the data.

Following the latest transaction, Ribbit Capital's combined stake in Groww declined to 6.91% from 8.29%.

Following the block transaction, Groww shares traded nearly 2% higher at Rs 231.30 apiece on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Wednesday, while benchmark equity indices were in the red.

In May, Ribbit Capital had sold more than 14.21 crore shares of Groww for Rs 2,567 crore.

item.title: Circular economy company Recove Ventures raises Rs 56.25 Cr
item.description: The company said that it will use the capital to build circular economy infrastructure in Maharashtra and expand Recove’s footprint in Karnataka.
item.content:encoded:
B2B circular economy startup Recove Ventures has raised Rs 56.25 crore in a funding round comprising Rs 36.25 crore in equity and Rs 20 crore in debt.

The round saw participation from Samara Capital Founder and CEO Sumeet Narang, Capri Global and Amit Prakash Sharma Family Trust (Sunrise Foods). Existing backers, including the family office of Chaitanya Kejriwal of Parksons Packaging and 5F World Chairman Ganesh Natarajan, also invested.

Recove will deploy the funding towards expanding its operations across India, with a focus on setting up circular economy infrastructure in Maharashtra and strengthening its presence in Karnataka, it said in a statement.

The investment will also go towards increasing industrial processing capacity, adding to its network of pre-processing facilities and developing technology to track materials and ensure quality.

The company has entered into 10-year MoUs with the governments of Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Uttar Pradesh. The agreements envisage investments exceeding Rs 500 crore in each state.

Including its existing commitments in Karnataka, Recove expects its planned investments across these markets to cross Rs 2,000 crore over the next decade.

The company is also exploring its next expansion opportunity in Uttar Pradesh.

“India's plastic recycling industry has a quality problem, not a recycling problem. The quality of recycled plastic is decided at the very start of the chain, at segregation, and cannot be recovered downstream. That is why Recove started at segregation and is building upwards from there to deliver consistent, industrial-grade recycled material at scale," said Viral Chhajer, Co-founder, Recove Ventures.

“Recove’s focus on segregation, processing and traceability addresses the practical challenges that manufacturers face when sourcing recycled plastic. Its network combines local sourcing with processing at scale—a strong foundation for serving customers reliably and building a commercially durable business," said Sumeet Narang, Founder & CEO, Samara Capital.

Recove uses digital tracking to monitor its materials. The company said this allows it to maintain traceability and quality standards across its supply chain.

Its operations include a plastic-washing facility in Harohalli, Bengaluru, which has been running since late 2025 and handles around 600 tonnes of post-consumer plastic each month. Apart from this, it has a granulation line at the facility which became operational in October 2026. In Pune, Recove has been operating a pre-processing facility for the past six months and is planning to set up three more.

Recove is now looking to scale its operations amid growing demand for dependable supplies of recycled plastic in India.

item.title: Inside MS Dhoni’s startup playbook: 13 companies backed by Captain Cool
item.description: From Garuda Aerospace to SolarSquare, explore 13 startups backed by MS Dhoni across fintech, electric mobility, gaming and clean energy.
item.content:encoded:
MS Dhoni's retirement from the Indian Premier League (IPL) as a player marks the end of an important chapter in his cricketing career. On November 17, 2026, Chennai Super Kings (CSK) announced that Dhoni would take up the role of team mentor from the 2027 season.

However, cricket is not the only field where Dhoni has built a presence. Over the years, the former Indian captain has invested in several Indian startups through personal investments and his family office, Midas Deals.

His investment portfolio spans fintech, drone technology, electric mobility, food, gaming, digital entertainment and renewable energy.

Here are 13 startups and companies backed by MS Dhoni.

1. Garuda Aerospace

Founded in 2015 by Agnishwar Jayaprakash, Chennai-based Garuda Aerospace develops drones for agriculture, defence, infrastructure and industrial applications. Dhoni invested in the company in June 2022 and became its brand ambassador. In February 2024, he acquired a 1.1% stake for Rs 4 crore.

2. Khatabook

Founded in 2018, Bengaluru-based Khatabook is a fintech platform that helps small businesses and merchants manage digital bookkeeping and daily transactions. Dhoni invested in the startup in March 2020 and also became its brand ambassador. The investment amount was not disclosed.

3. CARS24

CARS24 is a Gurugram-based online marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned vehicles. Founded in 2015, the company uses technology to simplify vehicle valuation, inspection and transactions. Dhoni invested in the startup in August 2019 as part of its Series D funding round.

4. HomeLane

Founded in 2014, HomeLane is a Bengaluru-based home interior design company that helps homeowners plan and customise their living spaces. Its services include modular kitchens, wardrobes and complete home interiors. Dhoni invested in the company in August 2021, although the investment amount was not disclosed.

5. EMotorad

Pune-based EMotorad manufactures electric bicycles for urban commuting and recreational use. Founded in 2020, the company aims to make electric mobility more accessible. Dhoni invested an undisclosed amount in the startup in April 2024 in exchange for equity and also became its brand ambassador.

6. Shaka Harry

Shaka Harry is a plant-based protein and alternative meat brand based in Bengaluru. It develops plant-based food products for consumers looking for alternatives to conventional meat. Dhoni invested in the company in 2022, although the financial details of the investment were not disclosed.

7. 7InkBrews

Mumbai-based 7InkBrews operates in the food and beverage industry. Dhoni became a co-founder, shareholder and brand ambassador of the company in April 2021. Its consumer brand, Copter7, offers chocolates and beverages inspired by Dhoni's iconic helicopter shot and jersey number seven.

8. Tagda Raho

Tagda Raho is a fitness startup that combines traditional Indian exercise techniques with modern fitness practices. Based in Bengaluru, the company promotes indigenous workout methods and fitness equipment. Dhoni invested in the startup in November 2023.

9. BluSmart

BluSmart was an electric mobility startup that operated an all-electric ride-hailing service and EV charging infrastructure. Dhoni's family office invested in the company during its pre-Series B funding round in June 2024. However, the company suspended its ride-hailing operations in 2025 following financial and regulatory challenges.

10. ACKO

ACKO is a digital-first insurance company offering products across motor, health and travel insurance. The company uses technology to simplify insurance purchases and claims. In July 2025, Dhoni joined ACKO as an investor and brand ambassador through his family office.

11. Kuku

Kuku is a Bengaluru-based digital storytelling platform operating across audio entertainment, educational content and short-form video. Its products include Kuku FM, Kuku TV and Guru. In March 2026, Dhoni invested in the company and became the brand ambassador for its microdrama platform, Kuku TV. The investment amount was not disclosed.

12. LightFury Games

LightFury Games is a gaming startup developing cricket-based gaming experiences for digital audiences. In 2025, the company raised $11 million in a funding round involving investors such as Blume Ventures, V3 Ventures, MIXI and Times Internet. Dhoni participated as a strategic investor alongside cricketers Jasprit Bumrah, Hardik Pandya and Ravindra Jadeja.

13. SolarSquare

SolarSquare is a rooftop solar company that provides residential solar installation and related services. Founded in 2015, the company helps households adopt solar energy solutions. In July 2026, Dhoni invested in the startup through his family office, Midas Deals, and joined as its brand ambassador as part of its $53 million Series C funding round.

Final thoughts

MS Dhoni's investments reflect his growing involvement in India's startup ecosystem beyond professional cricket. His portfolio spans businesses working in financial technology, electric mobility, drone manufacturing, digital entertainment and clean energy.

While the investment amounts and ownership details remain undisclosed for several companies, his involvement demonstrates how sports personalities are increasingly participating in India's entrepreneurial ecosystem.

As Dhoni transitions from an IPL player to a mentor, his business interests offer another perspective on his journey beyond the cricket field.

item.title: Nvidia chair says no plan to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: Late on Tuesday, in his first public statement since resigning, Huang said in a post on X that he would be honoured to return as CEO if the board decided it was in the company’s best interest. He also acknowledged making serious mistakes in his personal life.
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia’s board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, chair Harvey Jones said on the chipmaker’s earnings call on Wednesday. His remarks came hours after the co-founder said he would be honoured to return if the board decided it was in the company's best interest.

The board’s decision effectively closes the door on an immediate return for Huang, whose resignation has raised questions about corporate governance, national security, and the future leadership of one of the world’s most valuable technology companies. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and spent more than three decades transforming it from a graphics-chip manufacturer into a dominant supplier of computing infrastructure for artificial intelligence (AI).

“Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as President, CEO, and Board member. The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said, speaking at the start of the earnings call for the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

Jones said Huang had voluntarily resigned “after disclosure of personal behaviour inconsistent with the company's code of conduct standards and cultural norms”.

The board’s November 12 statement announcing his resignation did not provide a reason.

According to Nvidia’s regulatory filing, the resignation took effect immediately.

Jones said the board has retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to lead the search for a permanent chief executive. For now, Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO.

Kress, who joined Nvidia in September 2013, will continue as executive vice-president and chief financial officer alongside her interim responsibilities. The board is considering both internal and external candidates. Jones, who has served on Nvidia’s board since 1993, became its first-ever chairman following the leadership change.

“While this was an unexpected transition, the board acted deliberately and in the best interests of the company's employees, customers, partners and shareholders,” he said, adding that the board has “every confidence” in Kress’s leadership, integrity and ability to deliver as interim CEO.

Nvidia’s Board of Directors has established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, comprising a select group of independent directors, senior external advisers and legal counsel, to enhance the company's engagement with the US government and all relevant agencies.

The new committee will provide board-level oversight of national security policies, export-control compliance and global trade risks. It will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, while Nvidia’s National Security and Global Trade Compliance teams will report directly to the committee. The move comes amid growing scrutiny of the company's exposure to US export restrictions on advanced AI chips.

Huang’s message

Earlier, on Tuesday late night, in his first public statement since resigning, Huang said in a post on X that he would be honoured to return to the post if the chipmaker’s board decides it is in the best interest of the company, while admitting to serious mistakes in his personal life.

Since his departure, Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners and customers have called for him to return as CEO, and many continue to reach out to him directly, he said.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO… I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” Huang said, adding that he owns his mistakes completely and is committed to cooperating with the board's independent investigation.

US President Donald Trump also expressed support for Huang’s possible return, saying that he would not object to the board reinstating him. However, the board’s position remained unchanged.

More than 1.94 lakh people, including 9,788 who identified themselves as current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter seeking Huang’s reinstatement as of November 17, according to standwithjensen.com. Tesla CEO Elon Musk is among the prominent supporters.

Huang’s exit came days after media reports alleged that he had an extramarital relationship with a Chinese businesswoman reportedly suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing.

The woman was identified as Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based technology company Megaspeed International, which had business dealings with Nvidia. Reuters reported that Huang had misrepresented the nature of his relationship with her to senior Nvidia executives, describing their interactions as routine business dealings.

The board had opened an independent investigation following reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and US President Donald Trump said on November 8 that the FBI was also investigating the matter.

Separately, the US Departments of Commerce and Justice said on November 17 that their investigation into Megaspeed began in 2024 over suspected diversion of sensitive semiconductors. Nvidia placed the company on its internal “no-sell” list in June 2025, after US authorities requested information about direct and indirect sales to it. The Commerce Department subsequently conducted an inspection at Megaspeed in Singapore and interviewed its then chief executive, Alice Huang. The Justice Department later assumed the lead role in the criminal investigation.

The controversy has also reached Congress. Nvidia has agreed to cooperate with three US House committees examining the company’s dealings with Megaspeed and potential national security implications. Huang is scheduled to appear for a transcribed interview on December 1, followed by Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter on December 2.

Earnings

Meanwhile, Nvidia’s net income more than doubled to $65.3 billion for the quarter ended October 25, 2026, from $31.9 billion a year earlier.

Revenue rose 103% to $115.8 billion from $57 billion in the year-ago quarter and was up 20% sequentially. Revenue from the data centre business rose 110% year-on-year to $107.6 billion.

Data centre operations accounted for approximately 93% of Nvidia’s quarterly revenue, underlining the company’s dependence on demand for AI infrastructure from cloud-computing providers and other technology companies. Diluted earnings per share increased 108% to $2.70, while operating income rose 115% to $77.5 billion. Nvidia also announced that shipments of its next-generation Vera Rubin NVL72 computing platform had begun.

“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said in the statement.

For the fourth quarter, which includes an additional week, Nvidia expects revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

Significantly, the forecast does not include any data centre compute revenue from China, reflecting continuing US export restrictions and uncertainty over access to the Chinese market.

(With inputs from PTI)

item.title: Botsync raises $11M to expand industrial automation
item.description: Botsync has raised $11 million led by IvyCap Ventures to advance its AI-powered industrial automation platform, improve robotics capabilities and expand its presence in India and global markets.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore-headquartered Botsync has raised $11 million in a round led by IvyCap Ventures, a homegrown venture capital firm. 

Other participants include Capital 2B, a deeptech investor; Taiwan-based accelerator and venture investor AppWorks; South-East Asian early-stage investor Iterative; Singapore angel network AngelCentral; Genesis Alternative Ventures; and angel investor Nalin Advani. 

The round follows a January 2026 Series A extension led by SGInnovate, taking total funding above $20 million.

Founded in 2019, Botsync builds autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), or driverless material movers, and software that coordinates factory and distribution-centre operations. Its SyncOS platform connects robots, robotic arms, conveyors, machines and enterprise software, managing tasks and traffic through one interface. Its MAG robots move loads of up to 1.5 tonnes.

“As India’s manufacturing ecosystem evolves, solutions combining robotics, AI, and intelligent automation will play a critical role in driving efficiency and scale. We believe Botsync is well positioned to address this growing opportunity and expand its footprint across global markets,” said Vikram Gupta, Founder and Managing Partner of IvyCap Ventures.

Funds will add SyncOS tools for throughput optimisation, predictive maintenance and operational analytics, helping factories move goods more efficiently, spot faults early and use operating data to improve performance. Botsync will also improve MAG reliability, add Indian engineering and project-delivery staff, deepen local automation partnerships, and expand in Australia and the US.

India is both a market and capability centre, with a Bengaluru office and experience centre serving automotive and fast-moving consumer goods manufacturers. Chief executive Rahul Nambiar said the opportunity lies in “connecting robots, machines and software systems” so facilities operate more efficiently.

Botsync claims more than 70 projects across six countries, over two million production tasks and 99% uptime. Its customers include Caterpillar, Ford, Nestlé, Honda, Coca-Cola and Kimberly-Clark. The asserts some customers recover their investment within 24 months through reduced forklift use and manual handling.

The raise comes as robotics investment in India gathers pace, although from a small base. Tracxn data put startup funding at $63.2 million across 15 rounds by July 2026, compared with $26.7 million across 24 rounds in the same period of 2025. Recent deals included Unbox Robotics’ $28 million round in January, Armatrix’s $2.1 million in February and Anscer Robotics’ Rs 45 crore Series A in May.

Meanwhile, policy support is also building. In August 2026, four SAMARTH centres had reached more than 2,700 industries and trained about 33,000 people in Industry 4.0 technologies. The National Manufacturing Mission announced in 2025 prioritises technology access and workforce readiness, while NITI Aayog’s roadmap names robotics, artificial intelligence and digital twins as manufacturing enablers.

item.title: PhysicsWallah targets over Rs 9,000 Cr revenue by FY30
item.description: At its first Investor Day in Mumbai on November 18, the company targeted average annual revenue growth of about 25% or more between FY27 and FY30 and a pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin above 20%.
item.content:encoded:
Edtech firm PhysicsWallah said it is targeting Rs 9,000-10,000 crore revenue by FY30, an ambition that will test whether an online-first education business can keep growing while lifting margins and expanding its physical network.

At its first Investor Day in Mumbai on November 18, the company targeted average annual revenue growth of about 25% or more between FY27 and FY30 and a pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin above 20%. 

Pre-Ind AS EBITDA is its non-GAAP measure of earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. Online operations are expected to contribute about two-thirds of revenue by FY30.

The target more than doubles FY26 revenue of Rs 3,900 crore. Revenue from operations reached Rs 1,242 crore in the latest quarter ended 30 September. H1 FY27 pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin was 8.3%, against 18.8% in Q2. The company has noted that exam-related enrolments and course-fee recognition affect the timing of reported revenue.

Co-founded by Alakh Pandey and Prateek Maheshwari, PW began as a YouTube teaching channel in 2016 and became an education platform in 2020. Its offerings span test preparation, skilling, higher education and education-abroad programmes, delivered through digital content, an app and physical centres. It listed in November 2025. 

Pandey said, “We started PW so that no family has to choose between its savings and a child's education.”

Redseer estimates India’s test-preparation market at $14.8 billion in FY26, rising to $23-$26 billion by FY30 at annual growth of 12-15%. PW’s 25%+ target is faster. Redseer says families increasingly judge providers on teaching quality and reliable results, not reach alone.

Allen expanded from 43 cities in FY22 to 78 by FY26, taking coaching into smaller cities and adding AI-supported assessment tools. In September, upGrad completed its acquisition of Unacademy, highlighting consolidation after the pandemic-era boom.

Meanwhile, regulation is tightening. Central guidelines circulated in 2024 address coaching-centre registration, fees, infrastructure and student welfare.
